correctness.rationale: All 66 vertex pairs fall into five distance-signature orbits with fewer than 12 signatures; all 220 triples fall into 13 distinct S4 orbits, exactly nine of which resolve, totaling 156 bases. Two standalone checkers use independently encoded but explicitly isomorphic graphs, independent subset representations, and BFS versus Floyd-Warshall for all 12,090 unordered base pairs. Both establish 1446 jump and 450 slide edges, full connectivity and the stated exact distance, eccentricity and extra-cost histograms. A concrete failed matroid-exchange witness and seven-slide diametral path are exhibited. The claim covers only this finite graph and no infinite extrapolation.

value.rationale: The twelve-vertex truncated tetrahedral skeleton is a canonical vertex-transitive non-edge-transitive Archimedean graph, so its complete minimum-landmark mobility problem is structurally motivated rather than a random finite slice. The 13-orbit classification makes the exact 156 optima transparent. The Johnson-isometric jump graph is genuinely nonmatroidal, and restricting relocations to original graph edges introduces a sharp four-step detour on 204 pairs and a diameter-seven local-routing bound. Those contrasts offer a finite benchmark and boundary case for optimal sensor relocation under local motion.
